Beaded plant Suncatcher

Sunlight has a way of bringing a space to life. As it passes through a window, it fills a room with color, movement, and small moments that make a house feel like home. In this workshop, participants create beaded plant sun catchers inspired by the light that streams through our windows and the natural elements we welcome into our homes. By combining colorful beads and delicate forms, each piece is designed to catch and reflect sunlight, creating shifting patterns of color and light. The result is a decorative artwork that celebrates the warmth of home through nature, color, and light.

Small spaces can hold big discoveries. Designed for children under three with their parents, this environment is divided into three distinct zones: movement, hands-on exploration, and quiet play. A Home I Imagine

A home can begin as an idea and take shape in many forms. In this workshop, imagination leads the design process. Through drawing, building, and assembling materials, children develop their own vision of a home and translate it into a tangible model. Each creation results in a constructed home that reflects personal ideas and vision.

A story-led experience that follows Ajeeb as he visits a series of unusual homes, each shaped by a different idea, form, or function. The activity combines storytelling with creative decision-making, moving from observation to design.

Around the Table

An interactive activity where children explore how dining tables bring together different cultural practices. The program introduces a range of customs and habits from around the world, showing how the way people gather, sit, and share meals can differ from one place to another. Through simple role-play, children take part in everyday moments such as greeting others, welcoming guests, and spending time around a table.

Built by Nature

A bird&rsquo;s nest, a termite mound, a shell, each one is carefully built, not by chance, but by need. In this workshop, children observe how living things design their homes, then borrow these ideas to sketch and shape their own. Openings for air, layers for protection, and smart use of materials begin to appear in their designs. What starts in nature slowly turns into a built form.

My Family Bouquet

A bouquet grows, one flower at a time. In this hands-on workshop, children begin with simple shapes and watch them take form as each piece is rolled, combined, and built into a flower. As the bouquet comes together, each flower stands for someone at home, gathered into one arrangement shaped through making and choice.
